title: Interpretive rules and new legal duties
shortTitle: Interpretive rules and new legal duties
summary: An interpretive rule explains a preexisting legal obligation; a legislative rule exercises delegated authority to create or amend a binding legal norm.
notes:
American Mining Congress identifies indicators of legislative action: without the new rule, the agency would lack a sufficient legal basis for enforcement, or the new rule repudiates an existing legislative rule. The notes state that later D.C. Circuit law abandoned publication in the Code of Federal Regulations as a decisive indicator. Absence of an indicator does not settle every case.

Paralyzed Veterans sustained an explanation that wheelchair sightlines had to extend over standing spectators because the interpretation was fairly encompassed by the existing requirement of comparable sightlines. Hoctor rejected an eight-foot big-cat fence requirement as a policy selection that could not be derived by interpreting a general secure-containment rule. Numeric specificity may signal such selection, but the court expressly declined to classify every numerical interpretation as legislative.

Perez rejected the separate rule that an agency must use notice and comment whenever it changes a prior interpretation of its regulation. Section 553 exempts interpretive rules without that carveout. Perez did not resolve the broader, contested boundary between interpretation and legislation. This course account keeps the overruled change-of-interpretation doctrine distinct from the surviving inquiry into whether a purported interpretation adds a new duty.
